# pnpm Gotchas

> Known pnpm patterns that cause silent failures or hard-to-debug errors.

## Entries

- [Packages with legacy bundled types (bare `/// <reference types="node" />`) fail tsc under pnpm + nodenext](legacy-package-types-nodenext.md): npm-passing packages like winston-transport lose their `stream.Writable` base under pnpm's symlinked store + `moduleResolution: nodenext`; config fixes (node-linker, public-hoist, packageExtensions, preserveSymlinks) all fail, use a local type shim. HIGH.
- [npm install in a pnpm repo leaves stale physical packages that shadow pnpm's versions](npm-install-contaminates-pnpm-node-modules.md): stale physical copies at the node_modules root survive `pnpm install` ("Already up to date") and surface later as baffling version-mismatch errors (e.g. jest's `clearMocksOnScope is not a function`); diagnose with an isSymbolicLink() scan, fix with a full node_modules wipe + `pnpm install`. HIGH.
- [pnpm v11 ignores package.json `pnpm.overrides`, and range overrides DO re-resolve](v11-overrides-workspace-yaml-and-ranges.md): v11 reads overrides from `pnpm-workspace.yaml` only -- a `pnpm.overrides` block in package.json is silently ignored (install succeeds, lockfile unchanged, audit still fails), which mimics a failed re-resolution and sends you to the v10 exact-pin advice that cannot help. Ranges DO force re-resolution on v11 (pulled brace-expansion 5.0.8 under minimatch@3.1.5's `^1.1.7`); pin exact only when a parent's declared major constrains you (ajv's `fast-uri: ^3.0.1`). Scopes the v10-only typescript entry. HIGH.
- [`pnpm run <script> -- --flag` turns the flag into a positional argument](run-flag-passthrough-double-dash.md): the `--` separator npm requires is what breaks pass-through in pnpm v11 -- the flag reaches the binary as a positional arg, so `pnpm test -- --forceExit` hits jest as a test *path pattern* (0 matches) and the error blames your jest config. Omitting `--`, or `pnpm exec`, works; a named script is safest. Loud with jest, silent with any CLI that tolerates stray positionals. HIGH.
- [A stale workspace-package `dist/` blames your new code, not the build you forgot to run](stale-workspace-dist-blames-the-consumer.md): A private workspace package consumed via `main`/`types` -> `dist/` is resolved from build output by tsc, Node and Jest alike, and none of `npx tsc` / `npx jest` build it -- only the package script does (`pnpm --filter <pkg> build && jest`), so a gate copied bare out of a runbook or CI step silently skips it. The error then points at the consumer: `TS2724: has no exported member named 'X'. Did you mean 'Y'?` for a name plainly present in the package's src/index.ts, with the suggestion pointing somewhere worse; at runtime the same staleness is `Cannot read properties of undefined`. Both halves go stale together so tsc and Jest fail in agreement, which reads as strong evidence the code is wrong. Tell: the symbol is in src/index.ts and absent from dist/index.d.ts -- grep the artifact before debugging the import. MEDIUM.
- [`pnpm run` verifies deps against the workspace root, so `--ignore-workspace` on install does not scope the build](run-verifies-deps-against-workspace-root.md): `--ignore-workspace` scopes `pnpm install` but not `pnpm run` -- pnpm 11 verifies deps before running a script, and that check resolves the nearest pnpm-workspace.yaml ABOVE cwd, so a standalone nested package (own lockfile, deliberately not a workspace member) silently installs the entire monorepo before its build script runs. Invisible locally (root node_modules already exists, so the check passes silently). The damage is exposure, not the install itself: a job that never referenced the rest of the repo now fails on anything wrong at the root -- here a bad `dashboard/node_modules` symlink, surfacing as an ENOENT naming a package the failing job never touched. Tells: `Scope: all N workspace projects`, progress lines prefixed `../..`, and a `runDepsStatusCheck -> tryFrozenInstall -> linkDirectDepsOfProject` stack. Fix is `pnpm --config.verify-deps-before-run=false <script>` with the flag BEFORE the script name; placed after it, pnpm forwards it to the script and you get a different failure that looks like a different bug. HIGH.
- [`pnpm update` leaves the old version resolvable, so the suite passes green against the package you just replaced](update-leaves-stale-store-false-green.md): manifests and lockfile update correctly, but orphaned `.pnpm` store dirs and the hoisted `.pnpm/node_modules/` fallback keep the OLD version linked, so the suite passes against the package you thought you replaced -- a 39-package upgrade reported 1896/1896 green while still linked to tiptap 3.27.3, then the same commit failed with prosemirror-model "multiple versions were loaded" once the tree was relinked. Tell: a version present in `node_modules/.pnpm` with ZERO references in pnpm-lock.yaml is an orphan. `pnpm install --force` answers "Already up to date" and relinks nothing; `pnpm why` reads the lockfile so it reports one version while two are on disk. Only `rm -rf node_modules */node_modules` + `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` clears it. Distinct from the npm-contamination entry (that one is physical dirs from running npm, and fails loudly; this one is symlinks from pnpm itself, and passes). HIGH.
- [pnpm 12 records the package manager IN the lockfile, so bumping the pnpm pin without reinstalling breaks every `--frozen-lockfile` install](v12-lockfile-pins-the-package-manager.md): pnpm 12's `packageManagerDependencies` makes pnpm-lock.yaml a TWO-document YAML whose new first document pins `pnpm` plus all eight `@pnpm/exe.*` platform binaries -- coupling the lockfile to `packageManager` in package.json. Bump the pin (package.json, a Dockerfile stage, a `corepack prepare` line) without re-running `pnpm install` and you get ERR_PNPM_FROZEN_LOCKFILE_WITH_OUTDATED_LOCKFILE, "Cannot update packageManagerDependencies with frozen-lockfile". Invisible where you work: a plain `pnpm install` silently fixes it and reports success, so `test`/`build` stay green locally and the first thing that breaks is CI and every Docker stage, i.e. the deploy -- from a commit that passed. The error names a concept that did not exist in pnpm 11 and appears in no file you edited, so it does not point back at the version bump; there is no dependency drift to find. Fix: bump every pin site (`grep -rn 'pnpm@[0-9]'`), `pnpm install`, then prove `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` exits 0 BEFORE committing, all in one commit. Also: the lockfile is now multi-document, so single-document parsers (`yaml.safe_load`, `YAML.parse`) see no dependencies; the `@pnpm/exe.*` entries are recorded but never materialised under corepack, so they do not reintroduce the libatomic.so.1 dependency; and pnpm 12 now ERRORS on unrecognised pnpm-workspace.yaml settings instead of ignoring them. MEDIUM.
